title: Harrison's band breaks up and Alvin Walls's later career
summary: The band dissolves; Walls goes to Texas and Detroit and is said to have sight-read Fletcher Henderson's hard music; Harrison later dies in California.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: That job gave out, and Gordon Harrison -- we brought the band back to Little Rock, and we worked in and out and around Little Rock for a while. And then Gordon decided, well, he's going back home. So, he -- the band bursted up. But that

saxophone player was Alvin Pat Walls.
He later went to Texas and had a band of his own.
And then he finally left Texas. He went to Detroit, and he
played with some of the fine bands around Detroit. Fletcher
Henderson offered him a job many years ago and -- because he
was supposed to have been the only man that sat in Fletcher
Henderson's band and played every note by sight. Because back
in those days Fletcher Henderson was playing a lot of hard
music, and in a lot of hard keys back in those days.

I'll tell you a story about Fletcher Henderson that
happened in 1920 -- early -- in '27, the summer of '27 -- a
little bit later on, you see. Gordon C. Harrison came on --
he left Little Rock and went on back to Texicana, and a year or
two later he went to California. And he worked at a burlesque
theater out there until he died. I forget what year he died,
but he died, oh, about 30 some years ago he died out there.
